studies.Reference: Copper and zinc levels in plasma and cancerous tissues and their relation with expression of VEGF and HIF-1 in the pathogenesis of muscle invasive urothelial bladder cancer: a case-controlled clinical study.
studies.Title: Copper and zinc levels in plasma and cancerous tissues and their relation with expression of VEGF and HIF-1 in the pathogenesis of muscle invasive urothelial bladder cancer: a case-controlled clinical study.
studies.Authors: Mortada WI, Awadalla A, Khater S, Ahmed A, Hamam ET, El-Zayat M, Shokeir AA
studies.Journal: Environmental science and pollution research international
studies.Population: Muscle invasive urothelial bladder cancer patients and matched controls
studies.comparison_type: Urothelial (transitional cell) bladder carcinoma patients versus matched controls (plasma Cu levels)

sample_size.excerpt: Plasma levels of Cu and Zn were determined in 66 transitional bladder cell carcinoma patients (BC group) and 60 matched controls.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 66 + 60 = 126

cases.excerpt: To evaluate Cu and Zn levels in bladder cancer (BC) patients and their relationship with expression of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and hypoxia-inducible factor 1 (HIF-1). Plasma levels of Cu and Zn were determined in 66 transitional bladder cell carcinoma patients (BC group) and 60 matched controls.

comparison.excerpt: The results showed that plasma Cu and Cu/Zn ratio were significantly higher in BC group when compared with the control group.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Plasma levels of Cu and Zn were determined
